mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% for two consecutive months signals the Federal Reserve's impending tightening, which raises discount rates and reduces expected equity present value, thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% and remains > 0.3% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: early stages of a disinflation-to-tightening transition
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-trigger mean (p > 0.10), or FEDFUNDS remains below 1.5% with no subsequent rate hikes.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in FEDFUNDS below 1.5% for three consecutive months indicate a prolonged easing stance by the Fed, lowering real interest rates and boosting equity valuation sensitivity, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 1.5% and remains < 1.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in >70% of similar easing episodes (rolling IC < -0.05), or FEDFUNDS re-enters tightening before 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in PAYEMS (labor market strength) accompanied by a concurrent drop in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests a tight labor market, which can drive wage growth and corporate investment, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.1pp in the same month
failure_condition: Over 30 such triggered periods, SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10), or correlation between PAYEMS and SPX 5d returns is not significantly higher than zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeding 2% above prior month, coincident with a decline in RSAFS (durable goods orders), signals weakening near-term demand for capital goods and consumer durables, which tends to depress S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >2% in a month and RSAFS decreases by >5% in the same month
regime_hint: demand softening in capital goods cycle
failure_condition: In 10 such triggered episodes, SPX 20d returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.10), or the effect is explained by exogenous sector rotation (>40% of variance).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 3% for two consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which raises uncertainty and compresses growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >3% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: early signs of a supply-side contraction
failure_condition: During 5 such episodes, SPX 60-day returns are not statistically worse than average (p > 0.10), or INDPRO recovers before 60 days with no lasting effect on returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in HOUST (housing starts) exceeding 5% month-over-month, while UNRATE remains below 4%, suggests a resilient housing market and low labor market friction, which can support equity valuations and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% in a month and UNRATE < 4%
regime_hint: resilient housing market with loose labor conditions
failure_condition: In 20 such triggered periods, SPX 5-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10), or the effect is driven by energy sector outperformance (>50% of variance).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS below 1% for four consecutive months, coupled with a rising UNRATE, indicates a prolonged low-rate environment that amplifies equity risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for four consecutive months and UNRATE rises by >0.2pp in the same period
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns in similar episodes are not statistically higher than baseline (p > 0.10), or FEDFUNDS re-enters tightening before 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in GDPC1 below -1% while INDPRO remains flat or rising indicates softening consumption demand without supply-side weakness, which can create demand-side uncertainty and push S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by >1% in a month and INDPRO does not fall by >2% in the same month
failure_condition: In 10 such triggered windows, SPX 60-day returns are not statistically worse than average (p > 0.10), or the effect is explained by sector rotation (>60% of variance).
